decisions.issues: v12 is clean and matches the beat. The musket lies large in the foreground against the beam at the foot of the ladder, grey light comes down the hatch, and the chained pen rows face it with collar chains slack. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, bandaged wrists, and his left forearm is covered by bandage and manacle. Keshavrao also matches: short hacked hair, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, no stud. Minor points: Nagoji and Keshavrao look ahead rather than plainly down at the musket, and the background prisoners are nearly all bearded men who look alike. Both captions have room on the dark ceiling beams across the top (x 0.05-0.7, y 0-0.13), and the wet floor at lower right is also clear. Backup v10 is weaker. The musket is small in the lower-right corner rather than dominating the foreground, there is no ladder, and a highlight on Keshavrao's earlobe comes close to reading as a stud.

v09 is a proper close two-shot with Nagoji on the left and Keshavrao on the right. Nagoji looks up at the hatch, where water drips through at top left. Keshavrao looks off-panel right, toward where the musket lay in 2.1. Seawater threads across the boards around their bare feet and hobble chains. Collars, collar chain and wrist manacles are all correct. Nagoji has his moustache, only light captivity stubble on the chin, the gold stud, and fully bandaged forearms, so the brand stays hidden. Keshavrao matches his lock. Hands are sound. Minor points: they sit on the floor against the hull, not on the raised pen shelf seen in 2.1, and lettering space is tight. Usable space is the dark hull wall between and above the heads (x 0.42-0.58, y 0-0.25), the top-right strip over Keshavrao (x 0.72-0.85, y 0-0.08) and the dark right-hand wall (x 0.85-1.0, y 0-0.4). Backup v07 has correct characters and gazes, but it is a wide shot with the pair far apart rather than a close shot, and the water on the floor reads as a wet sheen rather than a thread of water.

Neither candidate is acceptable.

What both get right: the lantern-lit closed hold with barrels, crates, rope-wrapped posts and wet tilted planking, which matches 3.2 and 3.4. Nagoji is on the left with the thick curled moustache, clean chin with light stubble, gold ear stud, torn ochre tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged wrists, collar and ankle hobble chain. Keshavrao is on the right with short ragged hair, a faint moustache, no stud and a grey-brown tunic. Neither has text, gore or a noose.

v07 (new): the beat is lost and the anatomy is broken. Nagoji's two bandaged fists grip a stray extra cuff in mid-air, not Keshavrao's forearm. A skin-coloured stub sticks out of that cuff with a chain fixed to its end, so it reads as a disembodied hand fragment. Keshavrao has one cuffed right arm crossing his body to the barrel, but his far left arm ends at that same hand with no hand of its own. He clings to the barrel with no loss of grip shown. The irons are still tangled: Nagoji's near cuff chains to the stray cuff, not to his other wrist, and his collar chain drops down to meet his forearm.

v05 (previously rejected in r9 and confirmed as a major fault by the r2 five-lens review): Keshavrao's arms are at full span with unjoined cuffs. Nagoji's wrists are far more than a forearm apart, joined by a long loop that merges with his collar chain. A pale window-like grating shows sky at the top-left edge, and a black border is painted inside the frame.
decisions.correction: Keep the lantern-lit closed hold from the last attempt: hanging glass lantern, barrels, crates, rope-wrapped posts, wet tilted planking, no sky, no window, no grating. Keep the same faces, costumes, warm lighting and left-right placement. Simplify the pose and the irons as follows. Keshavrao, on the right, is sliding away down the tilting deck toward the barrels, having lost his grip. He twists back toward Nagoji with BOTH arms stretched toward him and his two bare wrists side by side, less than a forearm apart. A short chain of eight to ten links hangs between his two cuffs, visibly fixed to both. Nagoji, on the left, braces with his feet and reaches forward with both bandaged hands close together. One bandaged hand clamps round Keshavrao's bare forearm just above his cuff, fingers wrapped round the flesh of the arm. The other bandaged hand is right beside it. Nagoji's own short chain, about a forearm long and fixed to both of his cuffs, swings down and knocks against Keshavrao's cuffs. The grip area holds exactly four cuffs, one on each of the four wrists, with no extra cuff, no loose cuff and no chain ending in mid-air. Each man has exactly two arms and two complete hands, each hand on its own arm. Each collar ring carries its own separate slack chain that rises at a slant out of frame, Nagoji's to the upper left and Keshavrao's to the upper right, and never touches a wrist chain. Nagoji's left forearm stays bandaged from wrist to mid-forearm with the inner side turned away from camera. Do not paint a border or frame line inside the image.

decisions.issues: Pick v09. It is the first candidate that stages the whole beat. Nagoji (left) holds up the ring torn out of the splintered beam, and its freed chain splashes into the water. Keshavrao (right of him) hauls on a chain with one bare, cuffed foot braced. In the right half, a ring bolted into sound timber holds, and three collared prisoners have stopped and turn to stare after the pair. The setting is the closed, flooded hold: dark deck beams, hanging glass ship lanterns, no guards, no sky. That matches 5.4, 5.5 and 6.2. Both principals are on model. Nagoji has the thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, long curly hair, ochre tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged wrists, empty collar and hobble chain, and his left inner forearm is turned away. Keshavrao has hacked-short hair, a faint moustache, the grey-brown tunic, no stud and an empty collar, and both his wrists are manacled. There is no painted text and there are no painted balloons. The main flaw is minor but visible: Nagoji's raised right wrist has only a bandage and no iron cuff, so no wrist chain joins his two hands. If possible, touch up with an iron cuff over that bandage to match his left wrist. Smaller points: the collar rings sit at the front rather than the side (as in earlier accepted frames). Keshavrao's foot presses at the chain rather than clearly kicking the wood, and his hobble chain is only a dangling end. The water is ankle to shin deep, which matches 5.4 and 5.5 but is shallower than the thigh-deep water in 6.2. Lettering space: both balloons at the left fit on the dark ceiling beams. Keshavrao's 'Others.' can go first, in the gap between the two heads (about x 0.22 to 0.37, y 0 to 0.11), with Nagoji's 'Quickly.' in the top-left corner beside his head or just below 'Others.' above his shoulder. The captions fit over the plain dark water along the bottom (y about 0.86 to 1.0) or on the ceiling at upper right. v07 was not acceptable. Every figure hauls in the same galley-crew pose, no chain drops free, and no one is left staring. It is lit by open-flame brass dish lamps on posts, and it has a painted border. It remains the fallback only if v09 is refused.
